definition: Strangely out of place, or not fitting in with its surroundings or setting.
example: A flashing neon sign looked incongruous on the quiet stone cottage at the edge of the village.
nuance: Incongruous stresses a striking mismatch with surroundings; inconsistent stresses contradiction between statements or actions.
prompt: A guest arrives at a formal wedding dinner in an unusual outfit.
options: His muddy hiking boots looked incongruous beneath the elegant tuxedo.
After the long toast, the tired guest gave an incongruous mumble nobody could follow.
Her silk gown was incongruous with the formal setting, matching it perfectly.
Because the dinner began right on schedule, the evening was perfectly incongruous.
reasons: Dirty outdoor boots clash sharply with formal evening wear, so they seem out of place.
Speech that is hard to follow is incoherent; this word means mismatched, not unclear.
Something that suits its setting perfectly is fitting, the reverse of this word.
Starting on time is expected and fitting; nothing here clashes with its context.

practice.prompt: A history class watches a film set in ancient Rome.
options: The movie's running time was incongruous, lasting exactly two hours.
Students laughed at the incongruous wristwatch visible on one senator's arm.
The incongruous costumes were so accurate that historians praised every detail.
The incongruous student forgot to thank the teacher for showing the film.
reasons: A film's length alone says nothing about something being out of place.
A modern watch in ancient Rome is a glaring mismatch with the film's period.
Costumes that fit the era exactly blend in rather than standing out as wrong.
Forgetting to say thanks is thoughtless behavior, not a clash with surroundings.
